issues.description: New command names break the singular-dash convention used by every sibling command in the file.
issues.detail: Existing commands are quickmark-save, quickmark-add, bookmark-load (singular noun, dashed). This patch adds quickmarks-reload and bookmarks-reload (plural), introducing a second naming rule in the same namespace as a side effect of a four-line change. Rename to quickmark-reload and bookmark-reload to match the surrounding code.

issues.description: reload() mutates marks in place and leaves a half-empty manager if parsing fails midway.
issues.detail: reload() clears self.marks first, then re-parses via _init_lineparser. If _parse_line or I/O raises, marks is left empty, changed has not fired, and disk still holds the old data — observable state diverges from disk. Build the new dict from parsed lines first, then swap atomically and emit once.

issues.description: Feature scenarios are unnamed and only assert the info message, not that marks were actually reloaded.
issues.detail: Both new Scenario: blocks lack titles (breaking the file's voice — every other scenario is named) and only check that an info string appeared. They prove the command is wired, not that on-disk changes replaced in-memory marks. Name the scenarios and assert the resulting marks after mutating the file on disk.

issues.description: Unit test covers BookmarkManager only; QuickmarkManager reload path is untested.
issues.detail: test_reload exercises BookmarkManager.reload(). QuickmarkManager inherits the same method but overrides _parse_line and reads a different file, so the quickmark path is unverified. Add a parallel test, and consider a pre-reload assert so a regression where __init__ stops loading can't pass by accident.

issues.description: reload() races with the save manager and silently discards unsaved in-memory state.
issues.detail: UrlMarkManager registers a save-manager entry driven by the changed signal, so reload()'s emit will schedule a save of the just-loaded contents back to the same file. It also blows away any in-memory edits not yet flushed. At minimum document 'discards unsaved changes' in the docstring and reason about the autosave round-trip.

issues.description: Parse loop should be factored into a pure helper so reload becomes read, parse-to-value, swap, emit.
issues.detail: The skip-blanks/skip-comments/_parse_line loop is the actual unit of work and is now embedded in reload(). Extract it into a helper that takes lines and returns a dict; reload then reads, parses to a new value, atomically swaps self.marks, and emits once — values separated from effects. Optionally skip the emit when the new dict equals the old.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a small, useful patch with a genuinely good refactor — folding __init__'s parse loop into a reusable reload() is the right shape. But the work stops halfway: reload() mutates marks in place instead of build-then-swap, so a mid-parse failure leaves the manager empty while disk is intact. Command naming breaks the file's own singular-dash convention by introducing plural forms (quickmarks-reload, bookmarks-reload). Tests verify that a message string appears rather than that marks were actually replaced, feature scenarios are unnamed, and the QuickmarkManager path is untested. Verdict: salvageable, needs one more pass — rename to match convention, swap atomically inside reload(), document the discard-unsaved contract, and test the actual behavior.
